cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Sam 5:3), and he's talking straight to the LORD. His first words: 'To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul; in You, my God, I trust.' No small talk, no weather report, just his whole soul set right out on the counter.

cards.question: David trusts the LORD, and he has enemies around him. He asks the LORD to let those enemies gloat over him.

cards.text: Then David zooms out to everybody who waits for the LORD. And baker, I KNOW waiting, because I sat in a junk drawer so long the dust knew me by name.

cards.question: David says some people who wait for the LORD will still be put to shame.
David says those who wait for the LORD won't be put to shame. Who does he say WILL be disgraced?

answers.text: People who wait far too long
People who ask too many questions

cards.text: Then David goes from 'protect me' to 'teach me': 'Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.' That's a KING asking for directions, and me, I'd circle the block for an hour before I'd ask, and I don't even have legs.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to guide him in His truth and teach him. What reason does David give?

answers.text: The LORD is the God of his salvation
David has always kept the law
David is the one ruling Israel

cards.question: All day long, David ___ for the LORD.

cards.text: Next, David asks the LORD to remember one thing and forget another. I've been asking my own brain for that for YEARS, and it keeps every embarrassing moment and loses the timer.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to remember?

answers.text: His own compassion and loving devotion

cards.question: David asks the LORD not to ___ the sins of his youth or his rebellious acts.

cards.text: Instead he says, 'remember me according to Your loving devotion, because of Your goodness, O LORD.' Translation: don't go by MY track record, go by YOURS.
Then David stops talking to the LORD and starts talking about Him: the LORD is good and upright.

cards.question: Because the LORD is good and upright, David says He shows ___ the way.
David says the LORD guides the proud in what is right and teaches them His way.
David says all the LORD's ways are loving and faithful. To whom?

answers.text: Those who keep His covenant and decrees
Those who dwell within His holy city
Those who offer Him daily sacrifices

cards.text: Then David drops right back into asking, and he asks the LORD to forgive his iniquity, for the sake of the LORD's name.

cards.question: David tells the LORD his iniquity is only a small one.

cards.text: No 'it was barely anything, the dough was already like that when I got here.' He says it straight: 'forgive my iniquity, for it is great.'
Then David asks a question and answers it himself: 'Who is the man who fears the LORD?' I do that in the bakery all day, baker. 'Who ate the cookie dough?' Me. It was me. Case closed.

cards.question: What does David say the LORD will do for the man who fears Him?

answers.text: Instruct him in the path chosen for him
Give him a crown and a throne
Keep every trouble far away from him

cards.question: David says that man's soul will dwell in prosperity, and his ___ will inherit the land.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD confides in those who fear Him. The God who made EVERYTHING, confiding in people, and baker, I can't even get my oven to tell me when it's done.

cards.question: Besides confiding in those who fear Him, the LORD reveals His ___ to them.

cards.text: Now David says his eyes are always on the LORD, not sometimes, ALWAYS. Me, I can't keep my eyes on one batch for five minutes without burning it.

cards.question: David keeps his eyes on the LORD because the LORD will free his feet from the mesh.

cards.text: His feet are caught, but he's staring at the One who can free them, not at the mesh. Baker, I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I KNOW stuck.
Then the psalm gets quiet and honest, and David asks the LORD to turn to him and be gracious.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to turn to him and be gracious. What reason does David give?
David says the troubles of his heart are starting to shrink.

cards.text: He asks to be freed from his distress, and he asks the LORD to consider his affliction and trouble.

cards.question: Along with considering his affliction and trouble, David asks the LORD to take away all his ___.
David asks the LORD to consider his enemies, and he says they are only a few.

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to guard his soul and deliver him, and he says, 'let me not be put to shame.'

cards.question: David asks the LORD to guard him and not let him be put to shame. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He takes refuge in the LORD
He built the LORD a temple

cards.question: David asks that integrity and uprightness preserve him, because he waits for the LORD.

cards.text: And then, in the very last line, David looks past himself.

cards.question: In the psalm's last line, who does David ask God to redeem from all its distress?

cards.text: Not just 'redeem me.' Redeem Israel, from all its distress. I bet David knows his whole people need rescuing too, not just him.

findings.problem: The setup says David asks the LORD to 'remember one thing and forget another.' That gives away the answer to card 11, which asks David to ask the LORD not to ___ his sins, with 'remember' as the answer. 'Forget' also isn't the text's word. Verse 7 says 'Remember not.' 'One thing' is also off, since verse 6 names two things, compassion and loving devotion.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card only repeats verse 11. Card 17 already told it, and card 18 just asked about it. It doesn't move the psalm forward.

The card says David 'asks a question and answers it himself,' and the joke depends on that ('Who ate the cookie dough?' Me.). But verse 12 never says who the man who fears the LORD is. It goes on to what the LORD will do for him. So the 'answers it himself' claim, and the joke built on it, isn't true to the text.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'The God who made EVERYTHING' is a Bible fact stated with no reference. It comes from Genesis 1, not from Psalm 25.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This card only repeats verse 15. Card 6 told it, and card 7 just asked about it. Apart from the drawer joke, it doesn't move the psalm forward.
This card repeats verse 22, which card 19 just asked about, so it's a recap. 'I bet David knows his whole people need rescuing too' also supplies a reason for the prayer that the text doesn't give.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Several story cards are flat narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 13 and 17, and stop 2 cards 9, 12, 15 and 18. In stop 2 especially, the lonely, afflicted stretch (verses 16 to 20) runs as plain summary.

rule.text: A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
